core_obligations: Shrinking to a minimal counterexample (proof lines 1024-1036): for reductio assume the well-order A has no ordinal representation; if a proper initial segment also has none, replace A by the least such segment, so every proper initial segment of the resulting B has a unique ordinal order type.
Replacement construction (lines 1037-1042): f = {(beta, b) : b in B and beta is order-isomorphic to the initial segment B_b} exists as a function by Replacement.

Isomorphism verification (lines 1043-1052): ran(f) = B is immediate; f preserves ordering by the ordinal-segment lemma; dom(f) is transitive, hence an ordinal, and f : alpha -> B represents A, contradicting the reductio assumption.
proof_roadmap: Note uniqueness from the isomorphism-identity lemma.
Shrink to the least initial segment not represented by any ordinal.
Build the class of segment-order-types as a set f by Replacement.
Verify surjectivity, order preservation, and that the domain is an ordinal via transitivity.
Conclude the reductio: A itself is represented.
